author: NITESH DUBEY
description: Abhishek Sharma is on the brink of achieving a remarkable milestone, needing just 53 runs to cross 2,000 T20I runs during the second T20I against West Indies. With a chance to eclipse Suryakumar Yadav's record for the fastest attainment of this feat, Sharma's current high strike rate demonstrates his game-changing prowess.
title: Abhishek Sharma on the cusp of breaking Suryakumar Yadav’s unique T20I record

author: AMIT KUMAR
description: The young batter went on an attacking spree in the nets, repeatedly hitting the ball over the boundary and towards the stands. With every big hit, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi showed why he has become one of the most talked-about young batters in the Indian squad.
title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's explosive net session raises big question: Will he play in Ranchi?

author: AADRITA HALDER
title: 'Ready to do everything in our power': Putin offers to help end Iran war

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: A recent ruling upheld the Bowlin family's claim regarding a fence that served as a property boundary since 1967. This decision followed a dispute over the removal of the fence and trees by neighboring property owners. The Arkansas Court of Appeals affirmed damages of $12,000 due to intentional tree removal and ordered the reconstruction of the fence.
title: Arkansas family wins $12,000 after neighbours removed old fence and trees

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Richard Branson was 29 when he pursued an island to impress Joan Templeman, offering $100,000 for a property priced at $6 million before eventually buying it for $180,000. In 2007, he purchased 125-acre Moskito Island for $15 million. Today, the island has been divided among nine private families who own estates there.
title: Branson bought $6m island for $100k to impress girl, now worth millions

author: TNN
description: The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act, 2026, has come into effect on October 8. This Act mandates that senior posts in CAPFs be filled by IPS officers on deputation. The government supports this move for better coordination between the Centre and states. CAPF cadre officers express concerns regarding career advancement due to this new quota.
title: IPS quota in CAPF posts comes into force

author: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA
description: The Supreme Court stated that the appointment process for Jharkhand's DGP likely violated its previous judgment regarding officer tenure. The court issued a notice to Tadasha Singh, appointed shortly before her retirement. The Central Government argued that Jharkhand's amended regulations overstepped the Supreme Court's mandate on DGP appointments. Jharkhand, represented by Kapil Sibal, criticized the selective enforcement of these regulations by the Centre.
title: Jharkhand should 'revisit' DGP appointment rules, says Supreme Court

author: TNN
description: The Enforcement Directorate reported on a significant corruption case involving the Karnataka Public Service Commission. Candidates for the veterinary officers' exam were allegedly bribed to receive leaked test papers before the exam. An organized syndicate was involved in the manipulation of the recruitment process, leading to multiple arrests of officials. Investigations revealed a systematic approach to generating proceeds of crime through examination material leaks.
title: KPSC scam candidates taken to resorts, provided with Q&A: ED

author: MANASH PRATIM GOHAIN
description: World Bank's report reveals that unrestricted use of generative AI may enhance homework scores while diminishing actual learning outcomes. Evidence indicates that students using AI showed improvement in assignments but performed worse in exams over time. Concerns exist regarding students outsourcing their learning process to AI rather than engaging in cognitive effort. However, AI used by teachers to customize instruction shows promising learning gains.
title: AI use ups homework scores, but slashes exam marks: Study

author: ASHUTOSH SHUKLA
description: Madhya Pradesh high court quashed the preventive detention of two brothers under the National Security Act. The court criticized the reckless invocation of the Act by authorities and highlighted a lack of evidence. It found the brothers had been acquitted in multiple cases where NSA was applied, asserting non-application of mind. The court underscored the need for constitutional safeguards against arbitrary detentions.
title: ‘Reckless’ use of NSA has made it ordinary: MP HC

author: YASHASVI VASISTHA
description: Israel has announced that Captain Smit Machchhar will receive a prestigious Presidential Award for his bravery. He prevented a potential aviation disaster aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 by acting decisively against a radicalized co-pilot. During the incident, six Israeli passengers displayed great courage in assisting Machchhar and foiling the hijack attempt. This heroic act has led to a broader investigation into the circumstances of the attack.
title: Flydubai cockpit attack: Israel to honour Capt Smit with top civilian bravery award

author: BELLA JAISINGHANI
description: Nana Patekar, a renowned actor from Maharashtra, passed away unexpectedly from a heart attack in Goa. He was known for his powerful performances in both Hindi and Marathi cinema, spanning nearly five decades. Patekar had a notable impact on Indian cinema, often portraying characters that were unpredictable and emotionally complex. He championed various social causes, including rural distress through his NAAM Foundation.
title: ‘Krantiveer’ in life, ‘Natsamrat’ on screen: Nana dies at 75
